text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Iraqi press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
QADISSIYA
- Talks with the U.N. Special Commission continue in Baghdad.
- Iraqi foreign minister arrives in Amman on way to New Delhi for a non-aligned meeting.
- Israel backs Sudanese rebels with arms.
- India urges world superpowers to rid themselves of their nuclear arsenal.
- Washington ready to evacuate Americans in Zaire.
- Several Arab countries owe Iraq more than $1.4 billion.
- More preparations underway to mark President Saddam Hussein's birthday.
- New ship loaded with wheat under oil-for-food deal arrives in Umm Qasr in southern Iraq.
- National Assembly to hold new session.
(The above were also carried by AL-IRAQ and JUMHOURIYA)
- Article on how to improve maritime cooperation among Arab countries.
JUMHOURIYA
- Jordan and Iraq review economic cooperation.
- First deal to sell Iraqi gas to Turkey to be signed in July.
- Gulf newspapers attack U.S. policy towards Arabs.
- Editorial says 1997 will be a decisive year in U.N. disarmament activities in Iraq.
- National Assembly continues contacts to force Iran to free Iraqi POWs.
- International expert says Russia will become an economic superpower if it adheres to economic reforms.
